title: Father's schooling at a girls' college and his instruments
summary: His father worked as waiter and cook at a girls' school to study with its music professor, and became a reed specialist and good mandolin and banjo player.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: As a matter of fact, he gained his knowledge by accepting a job in a girls' college as a waiter and a cook, so that after the schooltime hours were out, where he served and cooked the meals, he could go to the professor of music in that particular academy and get himself a true education, which he did for a couple of years after hours, after his work was done.
What was the name of that school?
It was called Kitkey (PHONETIC) College. I think it was in Texas.
Do you know how to spell that?

K-i-t -- was the first name, and in Key, I think, was k-e-y. Because I've never seen it actually spelled. I just heard him speaking of it, speaking of Kitkey. But it was a girls' school actually, but there were some very fine professors there that knew what it was all about. So, that's how he happened to get his --
Oh, he was a young man. He was like 16, 18 years of age, and so that's how he happened to get his education.
How many instruments did he play?
Well, he could just about play anything that there was to be played, but he specialized in the reeds and he was, in that time, a very good mandolin and banjo player.
